text.p: This is how major world bond markets were trading in late European business on Friday.

GERMANY - Bunds erased gains on U.S. data. March retail sales were up 0.2 percent, below an expected rise of 0.6 percent, but the core rate was above forecast and February data was revised up. The June Bund future on the London International Financial Futures and Options Exchange (LIFFE) was trading at 99.84, down 0.27 from Thursday's settlement price.

BRITAIN - Gilts suffered losses in line with U.S. T-bonds after U.S. retail sales for February were revised up to 1.5 percent from 0.8 percent, indicating inflationary pressures could be mounting. The June long gilt future on LIFFE was trading at 108-20/32, down 09/32 from Thursday's settlement price.

FRANCE - French bond futures fell after stronger-than-expected U.S. data rattled bond markets worldwide but outperformed both U.S. and German bonds as benign French inflation and favourable monetary union comments sparked investor interest in cash bonds at the long end of the curve. The June notional bond future on the MATIF in Paris settled at 128.22, down 0.12 from Thursday's settlement price.

ITALY - Italian debt markets held in positive territory despite seeing their neighbours in the red following U.S. data which stoked concerns about the possibility of higher U.S. interest rates. The June bond future on LIFFE was trading at 127.39, up 0.26 from Thursday's settlement price.

UNITED STATES - U.S. Treasuries sharpened losses in late morning trade. The June Treasury bond future on the Chicago Board of Trade was trading at 106-16/32, down 27/32 from Thursday's settlement price. The long bond was quoted to yield 7.18 percent.

JAPAN - Key June Japanese government bond futures ended Friday's Tokyo session lower in choppy trade, after a stab at the upside faltered and dealers were forced to liquidate long positions, traders said. In after hours trading the June future on LIFFE was trading at 126.64, down 0.16 from Thursday's settlement price on the Tokyo Stock Exchange.
EUROBONDS - Issuance slowed sharply in anticipation of the key U.S. inflation and sales data.
The five-year dollar sector was the main focus this week and more deals are likely to surface there if bond markets are not badly hit by the U.S. producer price data.
